articles.title: Google’s bizarre new Gboard keyboard is a conveyor belt that brings the keys to you
articles.summary: Credit: Google TL;DR Google Japan has unveiled a DIY Gboard keyboard with keys mounted on a moving conveyor belt. Instead of moving your hand around a traditional keyboard, you can simply wait for the key you want to type to roll past. You can’t buy it, but Google has published the blueprints as open source, so you can actually build one. Google has once again decided that keyboards are far too normal. For its annual October 1 tradition, the company’s Japanese division has unveiled a new DIY Gboard keyboard that takes a rather bizarre approach — moving the keys to you instead of making you move your fingers to them.

articles.title: Samsung quietly launches the Galaxy Buds On, its first clip-on Galaxy Buds
articles.summary: Credit: Samsung TL;DR Samsung has quietly launched the Galaxy Buds On, its first clip-on wireless earbuds. The Buds On feature TwinBoost speakers, Audio Leakage Reduction, automatic volume control, and up to 9.5 hours of playback. They also bring Galaxy AI features such as access to Gemini Live, Quick Voice Memo, and head gestures, with a Korean launch set for October 27 at 299,000 won and a global rollout to follow. Samsung has quietly launched the Galaxy Buds On, its first clip-on wireless earbuds under the Galaxy Buds branding. The new wireless earbuds were quietly unveiled alongside the US launch of the Galaxy Tab S12 series and SmartTag 3 , although Samsung didn’t give them the same fanfare as its other new hardware.

articles.title: Plex makes content discovery a little more human on Android TV
articles.summary: TL;DR Plex is rolling out social features to the Android TV app. Users can now discuss, rate, react, and more. The primary menu has been relocated to the left-hand side of the screen. Tired of having an algorithm telling you what to watch next? Plex is bringing a human touch to content discovery. New social tools could help you find the next show you want to invest your time in. Today, Plex is rolling out social features to Android TV. These features include Discussions, Lists, Reviews, Reactions, and Follows. That means users on Android TV can now talk about what they are watching, create and share lists, rate and review titles, react to them, and follow other users. This way, you don’t have to solely rely on an algorithm for your recommendations.

articles.title: This camera company is taking over Google Photos’ Print Store
articles.summary: TL;DR Fujifilm is taking over Google Photos’ existing Print Store in the US. The store is now co-branded as Fujifilm for Google Photos Print Store, with Fujifilm handling operations, support, and the product catalog. Users still access printing through Google Photos. They’re getting more print formats, frames, décor, gifts, and select in-store pickup options. In addition to being your media storage gallery , Google Photos also acts as a gateway to the tech giant’s Print Store . It lets you order things like photo prints, photo books, and canvas prints directly from the app and the web, making it a convenient platform to turn your digital memories into physical ones. Functionality-wise, nothing is changing here. But there’s still a notable change behind the scenes that you should know about

articles.summary: Amazon S3 Tables now support all data types in the Apache Iceberg V3 specification. articles.title: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports metadata pre-filtering for higher recall on filtered searches
articles.summary: Today, we’re announcing metadata pre-filtering for Amazon S3 Vectors , which delivers higher recall on filtered queries by evaluating your metadata filter before the similarity search. You can filter on attributes such as tenant, category, status, or time, and pre-filtering adds prefix matching with $startsWith for paths, URLs, and hierarchical keys. Each vector carries up to 2 KB of filterable metadata, and a single query supports up to 100 filter constraints. There is no additional cost, no re-ingestion, and no change to your queries. Most applications never search a whole index. They search the part of it that belongs to a particular user, account, or category, and they express that scope as a metadata filter. articles.summary: About 66 million years ago, the Chicxulub asteroid smashed into Earth, kicking up tsunamis and dropping hot debris that annihilated non-avian dinosaurs and many other species. This space rock hit what is now the partially submerged Yucatan Peninsula, and at the bottom of the ocean, the impact generated enough heat to create a hydrothermal system that persisted for 8 million years and may have been a hotbed of life. When researchers drilled for samples in the impact zone in 2016, they studied the types of rock that had formed as a result of the asteroid strike. articles.title: Fifth unvaccinated person dies of measles; CDC still not counting all deaths
articles.summary: A fifth, unvaccinated person has died of measles in Pennsylvania, the state's health department announced Wednesday . The department identified the deceased as a resident of Lancaster County, which is the epicenter of a raging outbreak that began in late April. The updated case count as of Wednesday is 943 across 39 counties, including 119 cases reported in just the last seven days. At least 176 people have been hospitalized. Lancaster County has reported 381 cases and three of the five deaths in the outbreak. The previous two deaths were both in infants too young to be vaccinated. That includes a newborn boy and a 6-week-old baby girl . So far, no other information has been released about the county's third death announced today. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Returning from vacation? The government can search your phone without a warrant.
articles.summary: An Argentinian-American writer and immigration advocate recently sued the federal government, demanding that it delete data that he believes was copied off of his phone when he re-entered the United States earlier this month. According to the seven-page complaint , Thomas Kennedy said that a Customs and Border Protection agent at Miami International Airport physically searched his bags, questioned him about his books and magazines, and then demanded that he hand over his phone. “[The agent] threatened me, saying that if I didn’t give him my phone, my interrogation was going to take much longer and they could retain my phone indefinitely,” Kennedy wrote. “I felt like I had no choice, so I handed my phone to the CBP agent.” Read full article Comments

articles.title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails
articles.summary: Hackers have been exploiting a critical vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite in an attempt to obtain email backups and authentication credentials of vulnerable organzations, Microsoft has warned . articles.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon AI model, but you can't use it yet
articles.summary: Google promised Gemini 3.5 Pro in June, but it spent the summer trotting out smaller Flash models . Now, Google is ready to take on the frontier again with Gemini 4 Argon . The company claims this new AI offers industry-leading performance in coding, knowledge work, and cybersecurity, but you aren't allowed to use it yet. While most of us will have to wait to test Gemini 4, Google says engineers inside the company are already using the new model extensively. Argon reportedly used "fleet-wide telemetry data" to help Google save 300 TiB of memory across its data centers. Meanwhile, Argon agents have been working to migrate C/C++ codebases to Rust across Google, including thousands of lines in the core re2 and libgav1 libraries and more than 800,000 lines in the Fuchsia OS Zircon kernel. articles.title: Reddit is putting more limits on Old.Reddit.com
articles.summary: Soon, Reddit won’t let people use Old.Reddit.com unless they have used the site while logged in within the previous six months. In July, Reddit started requiring that users be logged in to access Old Reddit. This new requirement is an effort to reduce Reddit’s biggest source of scraping and automated traffic, the company says. Today, the social media platform announced additional upcoming restrictions on Old Reddit. A Reddit post from an employee, known as "judy-funnie" on the platform, says that “in the next few months, we'll further limit access for logged-in users to only those who have used Old Reddit in the last six months (which covers the vast majority of all Old Reddit users).” Read full article Comments

articles.title: RFK Jr. thinks AI will free us from the "tyranny" of medical facts, expertise
articles.summary: At a Make America Healthy Again event Tuesday, anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy opened a "fireside chat" with Vice President JD Vance on the topic of artificial intelligence. While MAHA generally coalesces around things like healthy lifestyles and mistrust of drugmakers, Kennedy quickly turned to extolling the potential of artificial intelligence, surprising Vance, who said he was expecting to discuss "weight loss and acid, not AI." Kennedy boasted that the Trump administration is "making it easy for every American to use AI," which he claimed would free us from the "medical tyranny" of doctors and health experts. He suggested Americans should start using AI to get second opinions about medical recommendations, saying AI is "better informed than any doctor in the country." H

articles.title: Trump plan to combat AI risks hinges on Big Tech pals policing themselves
articles.summary: Amid escalating AI security incidents causing OpenAI to halt training and pause releases , Donald Trump continues to advocate for the AI industry to regulate itself as the best path to combat emerging risks when developing frontier AI. In an agreement Tuesday, two dozen tech firms voluntarily committed to implementing controls recommended by the White House, including undergoing independent safety audits that will test whether firms’ internal controls, monitoring, and detecting are actually working. Key focuses for external reviews included “risks related to cybersecurity, biosecurity, chemical threats, and unintended actions by AI models.” Firms also agreed to regularly meet to discuss best practices and set common AI safety standards and benchmarks. articles.title: 商用逾30年C++編譯器前端EDG開源，C++ Alliance接手維護
articles.summary:
老牌C/C++編譯器技術供應商Edison Design Group（EDG）正式公開C/C++編譯器前端原始碼，結束逾30年的專有授權模式。後續專案由非營利組織C++ Alliance接手維護，既有EDG開發人員也會繼續參與，原始碼目前已公開在GitHub。
EDG的C++編譯器前端自1992年推出，而編譯器前端主要負責程式碼編譯的前置工作，負責處理語法、型別和程式結構，再把分析結果交給後續的編譯或開發工具使用。因此EDG前端不像GCC或Clang主要供一般開發者直接作為編譯工具使用，而是提供給其他軟體業者整合進自家產品。

articles.title: Microsoft強化Entra ID登入驗證流程，阻擋外部指令碼注入
articles.summary: Microsoft將自10月中旬起，強制在Entra ID瀏覽器登入流程實施強化版內容安全性原則（Content Security Policy，CSP），預計10月底前完成。在這項新政策下，僅允許來自受信任Microsoft CDN網域的指令碼執行，阻擋外部或未授權程式碼注入，以降低跨站指令碼（XSS）等攻擊竊取認證資訊的風險。

articles.title: 思科警告Catalyst SD-WAN Manager存在重大等級的身分驗證繞過漏洞
articles.summary: 9月30日思科發布資安公告，Catalyst SD-WAN Manager存在重大漏洞CVE-2026-76504，問題源自API連線階段（Session）的身分驗證管理，未通過驗證的攻擊者可藉此以管理員權限的使用者遠端存取Catalyst SD-WAN Manager，CVSS嚴重程度評為9.8分。思科特別提及，由於沒有其他替代緩解措施，加上已出現遭積極利用的情形，呼籲用戶應儘速套用軟體更新因應。

articles.summary: 企業要分析敏感資料，又不希望暴露原始資料，可採用不同隱私強化技術。非營利組織雲端安全聯盟（CSA）發布隱私強化技術指引，比較5種隱私強化技術（Privacy-Enhancing Technologies，PETs），分析不同技術在效能、信任需求、安全性及硬體需求等面向的差異。

articles.title: 全球前百萬網站54%支援PQC金鑰交換，CDN預設啟用成主要推力
articles.summary: 網路應用與資安業者F5調查全球排名前100萬個網站，發現其中54%的網站已支援後量子密碼學（Post-Quantum Cryptography，PQC）金鑰交換，但這波PQC採用成長主要受到CDN效應推動。Cloudflare、Fastly等大型CDN與邊緣服務平臺已預設啟用PQC金鑰交換；排除Cloudflare託管的網站後，PQC金鑰交換支援比例僅剩22%。

articles.title: The Hidden Challenges of Edge AI Design
articles.summary: Key Takeaways: Successful edge AI design requires prioritizing long-term architectural adaptability, memory bandwidth, and system-level efficiency over raw peak NPU TOPS. The mismatch between fast-evolving AI models and long silicon development cycles makes hardware-software co-design and heterogeneous compute increasingly important. Security must be built into the hardware from the start to protect against software supply chain risks, data breaches, and silent perceptual fault injection. The rapid buildout of the edge is forcing chip architects and design teams to rethink how they add AI to vertical market applications. articles.summary: Key Takeaways: Automakers are making different bets on compute architecture, with some favoring large central processors while others distribute specialized compute across AI-defined vehicle systems. Moving sensor data is becoming as important as processing it, with raw camera and radar data putting new demands on memory, interfaces, in-vehicle networks, and power efficiency. AI-defined vehicle systems must verify sensor inputs, AI decisions, and updates across edge cases and over a vehicle’s long service life. Carmakers are racing to develop and incorporate advanced AI capabilities into vehicles in order to capitalize on what is expected to be a $1 trillion-plus market for physical AI over the next decade. articles.title: Turning Edge AI Data Into Real-Time Action
articles.summary: Key Takeaways: Edge AI is expanding across consumer, industrial, automotive, and medical devices by moving real-time intelligence closer to where data is generated. Edge analytics systems deliver value only when edge devices have the right deployment, monitoring, lifecycle management, and software infrastructure. Security, power efficiency, connectivity, and memory choices must be designed in from the start as edge AI systems take on more autonomous decision-making roles. More AI is moving out of centralized data centers and into devices that can interpret data and act on it in real time. By handling more processing locally, these edge systems can sharply reduce latency, improve security and privacy, and address growing concerns about data center energy and water consumption. articles.summary: Humanoid robots are rapidly transitioning from research demonstrations to commercial deployment in factories, warehouses, and service environments. articles.title: Mitigating Threats With Pre-Silicon Security Verification
articles.summary: The safety and security of the silicon chips ubiquitous in modern life have become prime considerations in semiconductor development. articles.summary: By Kartik Sahajpal and Prashant Dixit Chiplet-based architectures are reshaping how high-performance systems are built, enabling designers to partition functionality across multiple dies in a single package for better scalability, yield, flexibility, and power efficiency. At the same time, PCI Express continues to remain one of the industry’s most trusted interconnects, delivering the software compatibility, transaction semantics, bandwidth scaling, and ecosystem maturity that modern compute platforms depend on. But as designs move from monolithic SoCs to multi-die implementations, conventional PCIe assumptions change, as chiplet systems require short-reach, high-bandwidth, low-latency, and power-efficient communication between dies inside the same package. articles.title: US Executive Order On Energy Grid Supply Chain Security
articles.summary: On August 26, 2026, President Trump signed an executive order declaring a national emergency to ban or restrict the acquisition and installation of high-risk foreign-produced equipment in the U.S. electric grid. It cites hidden cybersecurity vulnerabilities, malware and remote-access risks that foreign adversaries could exploit to disrupt critical infrastructure. The order affects equipment, hardware, software and firmware used in generation, transmission or control facilities operating at 69 kilovolts or above: large transformers, grid-tied inverters, circuit breakers, battery energy storage systems, SCADA software and industrial control systems among them. articles.title: Gemini Live’s camera just became much more useful for accessibility
articles.summary: TL;DR Google is rolling out Guided Vision in Gemini Live for blind and low-vision users. Gemini can describe what the camera sees and verbally guide users to reframe the shot when needed. Guided Vision works on Android 9 and newer in markets that support Gemini Live. For blind and low-vision users, pointing a phone camera at something is only useful if the phone can explain what it sees. Google has been building towards just that with Gemini Live for more than a year, first adding visual guidance that could highlight objects on-screen . And now the company is turning that idea into a more accessibility-focused tool called Guided Vision. Guided Vision is rolling out today in Gemini Live on compatible Android phones. Once enabled, users can share their camera and hear real-time descriptions

articles.title: Android’s controversial new sideloading rules are officially here
articles.summary: TL;DR Google’s new Android developer verification rules took effect on September 30 in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apps from participating stores must now come from verified developers before they can be installed on certified Android devices. Sideloading unregistered apps is still possible through Google’s new advanced flow, but it deliberately adds more friction. Android has always sold itself on one simple freedom that iPhone users don’t really get: the freedom to install whatever you want, from wherever you want. Google isn’t killing that freedom outright , but as of September 30, it has officially started putting a few more gates in the way — and Android users in four countries are the first through them. Google’s new developer verification rules are now in effect in B

articles.title: Your Pixel’s 80% charge limit has a hidden power user benefit. Here’s how to use it
articles.summary: I have a bad habit of using my phone while it’s charging. Most of the time, you’ll find me playing Sudoku, my favorite game for years. I know it’s probably better to just leave the phone alone and let it charge, but that rarely happens. And I’m sure I’m not the only one. Maybe you’re in the middle of a game, replying to work messages, or just need to use it for something important while it’s plugged in. The problem is that charging already generates heat, and using the phone at the same time can add even more of it — something your battery definitely doesn’t appreciate in the long run.

The problem is that charging already generates heat, and using the phone at the same time can add even more of it — something your battery definitely doesn’t appreciate in the long run.

articles.title: 3 reasons Googlebooks will succeed — and 3 reasons they’ll fail
articles.summary: Googlebooks are the the next evolution of Google’s Android platform — a desktop iteration to supersede ChromeOS and bring the Android platform to the big screen. It’s a big, bold, and bombastic plan, and it makes the first real new desktop operating system in years. And yet, I have a few thoughts (and concerns) about it. As a longtime Chromebook user, I’m excited for this new platform, but I also have a few doubts about its success.

articles.summary: I used to joke that every new technology came as a three-course CISO dinner: hype for the appetizer, hope for the main course, and harsh reality for dessert. Dessert was always bittersweet. Now, with AI, enterprises barely have time to finish the appetizer before the harsh reality arrives. OpenAI on Tuesday, for example, launched its  Decisions API  as a limited preview. But that’s a hosted API that focuses its Luna model on questions with predefined answers, while AWS is releasing a  downloadable model  along with the data and scripts used to train it. Frontier AI models, they warned, are “anticipated to exceed current industry expectations, fundamentally transforming both offensive and defensive cyber capabilities.” This isn’t theoretical; attackers have proven their ability to bypass safeguards. articles.title: AI coding agents leaked 13,000 screenshots, and nobody hacked them.
articles.summary: AI coding agents trying to work around a limitation in GitHub’s command-line tool ended up publishing more than 13,000 internal images to public repositories, according to an incident report Glow Labs released this week. The company calls the incident PixelLeak. Developers at more than 300 organizations were affected, including one of the world’s largest tech companies, a frontier AI lab, a major enterprise software vendor, and a Fortune 500 travel company, along with teams in cloud, healthcare, fintech, and government, and the exposed images are spread across more than 900 repositories. articles.summary: Building the app was never the hard part. Now, with AI agents assisting with development, teams complete applications and internal tools faster than ever. The problem is getting access to live operational data. Teams rebuild access rules and connections by hand for every project, as fast as they can, to unblock the build. Sometimes direct access is refused, so the build is forced to run on a copy: stale by definition, and a dead end for anything that needs to write back to the source. articles.title: Luma AI Bets on ‘Hybrid’ Future for Hollywood

articles.title: Carlyle Warns on AI Hype and Credit Risk Ahead
articles.summary: Amid the AI boom, private credit is pouring into data centers and hyperscalers, but the risks are real. Carlyle's Co-President Mark Jenkins joins Bloomberg Open Interest with a warning that concentration in a single hot theme can mirror the "SaaS apocalypse," where everything looked diversified until volatility hit. articles.title: Are We Losing Control of AI? What’s Driving New Fears
articles.summary: For years, as artificial intelligence has evolved from the stuff of sci-fi movies to an app ordinary people have installed on their phones, tech leaders and some AI insiders have talked about the potential for it to escape human control and wreak havoc on society. Those fears have become impossible to ignore in recent weeks, driven by advances in the technology, a series of cybersecurity breaches involving AI agents, and new warnings from rank-and-file AI staffers.

articles.title: Marvel releases one last VisionQuest trailer
articles.summary: With its premiere just two weeks away, Marvel Studios has dropped one last trailer for the limited series, VisionQuest , which will complete the trilogy begun with WandaVision and Agatha All Along. (Spoilers for WandaVision and Agatha All Along below.) As previously reported , Marvel’s streaming TV portfolio has kind of been all over the place: a handful of hits, a few misses, and a bunch of middling offerings. One standout was WandaVision , followed by an excellent sequel (of sorts), Agatha All Along . VisionQuest will complete the trilogy. Vision (Paul Bettany) died in Infinity War , but WandaVision resurrected an all-white version whose memories were restored in the finale. We finally get to learn what happened afterward. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Memory executives expect RAM shortage to continue through 2028
articles.summary: Micron and Samsung executives this week said the memory shortage will continue for at least the next couple of years. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra expects demand for the firm’s memory to exceed its available supply over that period, he told investors last night. Micron no longer sells consumer RAM, and Mehrotra’s statements refer to Micron’s business-to-business sales of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI and DRAM for servers. However, his comments also have implications for consumer devices. Manufacturing capacity is prioritizing memory for AI and servers, limiting the supply of memory manufactured for consumer devices. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Florida cops say they don't know who owns 11 unpermitted Flock cameras
articles.summary: Florida cops are facing questions after a mandate to remove all Flock cameras tracking cars on St. Lucie County roads led local police to uncover more than a dozen suspicious cameras operating without permits. Local residents told The Washington Post that they were alarmed that no one knows who owns many of the mysterious cameras. Of the 14 cameras found, 11 had no obvious owners, raising concerns about who has access to sensitive data that bad actors could abuse. After the cameras were discovered, St. Lucie County Commissioner James Clasby told a local news outlet that there’s “potential for non-law enforcement to have cameras out there, and I’m not OK with that.” Read full article Comments

articles.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI—until now
articles.summary: Deep Blue took down Garry Kasparov at chess in 1997, AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol at Go in 2016, and poker bots have been beating professionals for years. But one classic game called Stratego held out. Even DeepMind, with its exceptional budget, couldn't build a machine that reliably beat the best human players. Now, a team of researchers from Carnegie Mellon, MIT, New York University, and Stanford University has done it. Their AI, called Ataraxos, beat Pim Niemeijer, arguably the best Stratego player of all time, 15 games to one, with four draws. And it took just 16 GPUs and a few thousand dollars to train it. articles.summary: For a long time, PC gamers could access many PlayStation 5 games only if the publisher invested in a bespoke port (something Sony has recently said it will be scaling back ). articles.title: 臺北市政府網站9/26服務中斷事件：跳電後機房過熱造成儲存設備關閉，備援分級成關注焦點
articles.summary:
臺北市政府網站在上周六(9/26)晚間一度出現無法連線情況，影響包括市府全球資訊網、部分局處網站及使用市府雲平臺的相關服務受到影響。臺北市政府資訊局後續調查指出，事件起因並非資安攻擊，而是市政大樓施工造成電力過載跳電，進一步導致資訊機房環境升溫，部分儲存設備因過熱啟動保護機制並關閉，造成雲平臺網站服務中斷。
根據資訊局的說明，9月26日晚間7點多，市政大樓地下1樓中控室因施工導致電力過載，引發跳電。跳電後，市政大樓10樓的資訊機房溫度升高，約晚間8點30分起，機房內單一儲存設備類型因過熱啟動保護機制停止運作，導致相關雲平臺網站服務受到影響。

articles.summary:
日本上市公司GMO Internet Group旗下、擁有日本大型白帽駭客團隊的GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae，於10月初發布新聞稿，宣布投資2020年成立的臺灣資安新創TRAPA Security（菱鏡公司，以下簡稱TRAPA），同時取得其攻防演練平臺「TRAPA CYBER RANGE」在日本的獨家代理權。
臺灣AI資安公司奧義賽博（CyCraft）先前也宣布參與TRAPA增資，認購金額超過3,000萬元，完成後將持有TRAPA完全稀釋後10%的股權。

articles.title: 中國駭客UAT-11587鎖定臺灣學術界與智庫，以圖片仿製Gmail附件預覽介面並用政府文件作為誘餌
articles.summary: 臺灣學術界、智庫與公民社會政策社群今年3月遭中國駭客UAT-11587鎖定，攻擊者透過魚叉式網釣接觸目標，目的是散布後門Antino，並在郵件中仿製Gmail原生附件預覽介面，將惡意連結包裝成看似正常的Gmail附件縮圖，不同攻擊活動還會搭配量身設計的誘餌文件，例如以資訊戰工作坊資料及政府公開文件作為網釣題材。這波鎖定臺灣的攻擊，也成為Cisco Talos追查一系列網路間諜活動的重要線索；研究人員後續擴大調查後發現，相關攻擊最早可追溯至2025年9月，且已涵蓋多個亞洲國家。

articles.title: OpenPoint推出AI生活服務平臺，導入AI Agent線上預約餐廳、居家清潔與藥局領藥等12項服務
articles.summary:
過去消費者要安排生活服務，往往需要在不同平臺間切換：訂餐廳要找訂位平臺，居家清潔要找服務業者，領藥則需要確認附近藥局與服務流程。隨著AI Agent發展，企業開始嘗試讓使用者不再逐一操作不同服務，而是直接提出需求，由AI協助完成後續流程。
統一資訊今天(10/1)發表OpenPoint上的生活服務平臺「i住家」，將AI Agent的代理人概念導入到生活服務平臺。使用者可以透過文字輸入或語音說出需求，背後的LumineOne AI會理解語意，將需求拆解成工作任務，再搜尋平臺上可提供的服務，找出符合需求的選項。
